Hi Amy,

Thanks again for the time today — good to align on timelines for the pilot. You asked for a clear way to present the compliance add-ons to Procurement so they can sign without delaying the pilot. Two common commercial patterns we see and what they'd look like for SmallWell: one-time implementation/onboarding fee versus a monthly credit amortized across the first 12 months.

Quick sketch (pilot = 3 months, then scale):
- Audit logs (90-day vs 3-year retention): one-time indexing/setup cost vs per-month retention surcharge.
- KMS/HSM: either an HSM seat (annual) or a throughput-based pass-through; HSM seat tends to have upfront provisioning time.
- Data residency: per-region residency surcharge (one-time + small recurring).

If you prefer, I can send a side-by-side with the exact invoice math and the SOW stub. Would Procurement prefer amortized credits (so the line shows as a recurring offset) or a single upfront line item?

I can loop in Laura to put formal numbers against each path.

Thanks,

Thanks Amy — adding Laura (Sales Ops) and Marissa (Solutions) to put numbers to this. Quick answers up front: credits can be applied as invoice-level credits that offset hosted usage (we'll show it as a negative line on invoices), and HSM lead time is typically 4–6 weeks for provisioning + attestation. We can offer a hybrid path to avoid a full seat upfront: temporary software-level KMS for pilot + option to convert to a dedicated HSM seat at scale.

Option A — Upfront implementation fee (one-time invoice):
- Onboarding & audit-log ingestion setup: $45,000 (covers engineering migration, 90->365 day indexing scripts).
- HSM seat procurement facilitation + initial config: $25,000 (one-time).
- Data residency enablement (region setup): $10,000 (one-time).
- Total one-time: $80,000

Option B — Monthly credit amortization (12 months):
- Equivalent amortized credit: $6,700/month credit applied to hosted usage invoices for 12 months (netting to ~$80k).
- KMS: $2,000/month for managed KMS during pilot; option to swap to HSM seat later (conversion credit applied).

Notes:
- We can tier audit-log retention so that 90-day is included in pilot discount; 1–3 year retention is a separate per-GB monthly surcharge.
- We usually structure credits to reduce the invoice amount directly; procurement needs to confirm whether they want credits on each month or a prepaid invoice and refund schedule.

I've attached a concise workbook with line-by-line math and a SOW stub we can drop into DocuSign once numbers are agreed. Laura — can you confirm if the credit will show as a negative hosted line item in your typical terms?

Ben

Hi Amy / Procurement team —

Happy to confirm the accounting treatment and a recommended commercial structure. We typically support both models; below is the commercial language we put in the SOW to keep procurement comfortable and avoid timing friction.

Recommended structure for SmallWell (keeps OPEX flatter and reduces PO friction):
- Execute SOW that lists the full implementation cost ($80,000) as an "Onboarding & Residency Setup" line.
- Redwood issues a monthly invoice for hosted usage; the implementation cost is applied as a monthly credit ("Implementation Credit") that reduces those hosted invoices over the first 12 billing cycles until fully amortized.

Milestone credit schedule (optional, if Procurement wants milestone gating):
- 50% applied at SOW execution (appears as credit on first hosted invoice).
- 25% applied at pilot go-live (credit applied next hosted invoice).
- 25% applied at production readiness (final credit applied).

HSM path: we can include a conversion credit if you start on managed KMS and later move to a dedicated HSM seat. Lead time note: dedicated HSM seat provisioning and attestation is ~4–6 weeks; we can provision a managed KMS for pilot to keep you moving.

DocuSign: once we have the sign-off on amortization approach, Ben will send the SOW as a DocuSign with the standard commercial appendix. HubSpot record: 67890 (DL-3441).

Marissa — please prepare a short one-page onboarding checklist and an HSM vs KMS appendix for Amy; include an architecture diagram for their security review.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
